title: fling reprex on the internet e.g. as a gist
description:
Code snippet exchange are being quite popular as reprex for issue filing, shared example or other needs. Currently, they are published most often on SO, GH and Rstudio community, and mainly used as minimal reprex, so short snippet. 

Sometimes, reprex can be long on purpose (not minimal reprex) and it could worth being published online for isolation, reuse or just clarity. 

A gist seems to me very similar to a code snippet or example, and I used some gist sometimes for that. I think it could be interesting to be able to publish a reprex as a gist containing the source code and the files to create the reprex.

There is one example in this [gist](https://gist.github.com/cderv/46b10e13fe46743228a66ab6410dc530) where I wanted to publish some code examples online, related to [this discussion](https://github.com/tidyverse/purrr/pull/502#issuecomment-387110699) but outside. For this one, I took the yaml front matter used for reprex to generate the md file and use `gistr` :package: to render and publish, as this package has rendering hability like reprex.
```r
callr::r(function() {
  gistr::gist_create("map_flat_use_case.R", description = "map_flat usage examples", 
                     knit = TRUE, include_source = TRUE)
}, show = TRUE)
```
In this case, the R script and the md file are published in the same gist. Reprex is a great way to create quickly a reproductible code using R code and markdown, even for long script. Using Rmd format could have been another way, publish the Rmd file and the md output. But it felt easier to use reprex.

I think it could be useful to have in reprex such a feature of pusblishing results as a gist and retrieve the url to copy-paste somewhere. This would help sharing reprex more easily, even for minimal reprex.

What do you think on this feature ? Is a gist the correct tool for publishing ?

For this `gistr` can help and `gistfo` can be of inspiration. 

Questions identified: 
+ Which file to publish : R script with user code ?, R script created by reprex ?, code as Rmd file ? md output only ?
+ How to deal with external files ? (mainly images, but I think it is ok through imgur
+ Should it provide a way to update the gist ? 
 
 I can work further on something (i.e a POC) if you want.

title: Issues with last line of expression in Positron
description:
I am observing issues with the last line of the expression fed to `reprex()` when executing the reprex from an editor tab in Positron. These might be 2 unrelated issues but both seem to be related to the handling of the last code line by `reprex()`. Maybe Positron is at fault, I'm posting here as I was not able to reproduce the issue with anything but `reprex()`.

# Issue 1:

When the reprex call starts on the first line of the file, the last line of the expression is repeated in the temporary `.md` file. If the last line is a closing parenthesis for example, this will lead to the code failing in the reprex, while it works fine if the expression is executed on its own.

This:

```
reprex::reprex({
  library(
    reprex
  )
})
```

Turns into this:

``` r
library(
  reprex
)
)
#> Error in parse(text = input): <text>:4:1: unexpected ')'
#> 3: )
#> 4: )
#>    ^
```

- If I execute the whole file (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) it works fine.
- But if I execute the code with Ctrl+Enter the last line duplication occurs.
- Adding an empty line or a line with any content above the reprex call -> works fine

Reprex call in line 1:

```
reprex::reprex({
  "first line"
  "last line"
})
```

Reprex output:

``` r
"first line"
#> [1] "first line"
"last line"
#> [1] "last line"
"last line"
#> [1] "last line"
```

Reprex call in line 2:

```
"something in line 1"
reprex::reprex({
  "first line"
  "last line"
})
```

Reprex output:

``` r
"first line"
#> [1] "first line"
"last line"
#> [1] "last line"
```

# Issue 2

When I have an editor tab with two consecutive `reprex()` calls and I am stepping through the code with Ctrl+Enter the second one errors and the backtrace points to the part of the reprex source code that handles the last line of the expression.

```
reprex::reprex({
  "call a: first line"
  "call a: last line"
})
reprex::reprex({
  "call b: first line"
  "call b: last line"
})
```

```
Error in `if (grepl("^\\s*#", rescue_me)) ...`:
! argument is of length zero
    ▆
 1. └─reprex::reprex(...) at [tkrenz/Desktop/test_reprex.R:6:1](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html#)
 2.   └─reprex:::reprex_impl(...)
 3.     └─reprex:::stringify_expression(x_expr)
```

# Other observations

- None of these issues occur in RStudio or when I execute the reprex calls directly in the R console.
- When I first started to investigate this, Issue 1 seemed to be resolved by deactivating "Format on Save" in Positron. Later on I was able to reproduce with that setting active and deactivated.
- I am using Positron 2026.03.0 build 212 and reprex 2.1.1 and got the same outcomes on macOS and archlinux.

title: Reprex support for webr and Shinylive REPLs
description:
Tagging @jennybc and @georgestagg. Sorry, if this is the wrong place for this feature request/idea. Please ignore this if it is outside of scope. It would be convenient if there was a separate package or set of unctions to easily generate webr or Shinylive REPL URLs based on code snippets. Users could then share the URL with colleagues and let them directly run the code in the browser. The R version and the R packages supported might be a limitation, if user's systems aren't in sync with the REPL. 

Here's a small R package as a proof of concept that I made recently: https://github.com/parmsam/reprex.webr

title: `simplify_image_links()` fails to simplify because of unexpected html comment strings
description:
The function that is supposed to simplify the image strings expects strings of the form `![](https://i.imgur.com/woc4vHs.png)`.

https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/blob/07cd5d74fd25005523a57db97589ff8c3e74c02f/R/reprex_render.R#L335-L339

If this was the input, the code would work fine

``` r
x <- "![](https://i.imgur.com/woc4vHs.png)"
sub("(^!\\[\\]\\()(.+)(\\)$)", "\\2", x, perl = TRUE)
#> [1] "https://i.imgur.com/woc4vHs.png"
```

However, the actual input includes empty html strings and has the form `![](https://i.imgur.com/woc4vHs.png)<!-- -->`

In this case, the function fails to simplify the link 
``` r

x <- "![](https://i.imgur.com/woc4vHs.png)<!-- -->"
sub("(^!\\[\\]\\()(.+)(\\)$)", "\\2", x, perl = TRUE)
#> [1] "![](https://i.imgur.com/woc4vHs.png)<!-- -->"
```

The result is that links aren't simplified when doing `reprex(venue = "slack")`  as the below example shows (I put the image link in backticks)

```
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, qsec)) +
  geom_point()

tmpfile <- tempfile()

title: findCorrelation_exact with problem in the variable selection
description:
Since the commit `f2ad13509ba3d6ab28069840c9631a66a9e7ecc8` the function `findCorrelation_exact` in the row 38 are computing the wrong mean absolute correlation to the `mn2`. The function are calculating the mean of the matrix without the variable `j` instead of calculate the mean of variable `j` against the another variables.

Have 2 possible solutions, the first one is remove the minus sign of the `j`, so you will compare 2 different rows of the matrix, but the output when the `verbose = TRUE` prints: "Compare row i and column  j with corr..." and even if the row and column are mirrored(the same) this is a incorrect text. Then we have the second option: remove the minus sign and change the j to the column position.

```r
#before the commit
(mean(x[i, -i]) > mean(x[-j, j]) #compare the mean of two vectors
#after the commit
mn1 <- mean(x2[i,], na.rm = TRUE) #return the mean of a vector
mn2 <- mean(x2[-j,], na.rm = TRUE) #return the mean of a matrix
#possible solution 1
mn2 <- mean(x2[j,], na.rm = TRUE) #return the mean of the row 
#possible solution2
mn2 <- mean(x2[, j], na.rm = TRUE) #return the mean of the column
```
reprex:

``` r
require(tidyverse)
#> Carregando pacotes exigidos: tidyverse

iris <- datasets::iris
cor_mat <- as.matrix(iris[,1:4]) %>% cor()

#Finding correlation manually ----
## Example with row 3 and column 4 ----
diag(cor_mat) <- NA
cor_mat <- abs(cor_mat)
i <- 3 #simulating the i-th iteraction when i = 3
j <- 4 #simulating the j-th iteraction when j = 4

mn1 <- mean(cor_mat[i,], na.rm = TRUE)
mn2 <- mean(cor_mat[,j], na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Compare row", i, " and column ", j,
    "with corr ", round(cor_mat[i,j], 3), "\n",
    "  Means: ", round(mn1, 3), "vs", round(mn2,3))
#> Compare row 3  and column  4 with corr  0.963 
#>    Means:  0.754 vs 0.716

## Example with row 4 and column 1 ----
cor_mat[3,] <- NA #removing row 3 and column 3 to simulate the iteraction of the function, based on the previous step
cor_mat[,3] <- NA

i <- 4 #simulating the i-th iteraction when i = 3
j <- 1 #simulating the j-th iteraction when j = 4

mn1 <- mean(cor_mat[i,], na.rm = TRUE)
mn2 <- mean(cor_mat[,j], na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Compare row", i, " and column ", j,
    "with corr ", round(cor_mat[i,j], 3), "\n",
    "  Means: ", round(mn1, 3), "vs", round(mn2,3))
#> Compare row 4  and column  1 with corr  0.818 
#>    Means:  0.592 vs 0.468

#Finding correlation with findCorrelation_exact ----
iris <- datasets::iris
cor_mat <- as.matrix(iris[,1:4]) %>% cor()

vars_cor <- caret::findCorrelation(
    cor_mat,
    cutoff = 0.7,
    names = T,
    exact = T,
    verbose = T)
#> Compare row 3  and column  4 with corr  0.963 
#>   Means:  0.754 vs 0.554 so flagging column 3 
#> Compare row 4  and column  1 with corr  0.818 
#>   Means:  0.592 vs 0.417 so flagging column 4 
#> All correlations <= 0.7
```

title: Ensure white background when rendering via `reprex:::preview()`
description:
This is an issue in visual display that first caught my eye transitioning form RStudio to Positron. I wasn't sure (and am still not quite sure) whether this issue belongs here or in Positron, but I decided to post here after a detour investigation (more details in this thread https://fosstodon.org/@yjunechoe/112997187221404762)

I'm a dark mode IDE user. In RStudio, reprexes have always rendered in the Viewer panel with a white background, regardless of editor theme. But in Positron, I'm seeing reprexes render with transparent background, and dark background sets a bad contrast against the contents of the reprex.

```r
reprex::reprex("1")
```

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/738429ef-7d84-414d-800d-6a287a060455)


Maybe this reflects a fundamental difference in how RStudio and Positron render Github flavored markdown in the Viewer. But in any case I can confirm that just injecting the `background: white;` css somewhere in the document can prevent the reprex from visually blending into the IDE background. So it would be nice if `reprex:::preview()` could guarantee a white-background hml at least when rendering interactively to the viewer, if that's a desirable behavior to hard-code.

title: Enhance `would_clobber()` with more help getting rid of the offending file

`would_clobber()` could potentially do more in both interactive and non-interactive sessions:

* Could use a cli hyperlink for runnable code to delete the file that's blocking things. (It would not be automatically runnable, but would still get some nice affordances to make it easily runnable.)
* Could even offer to delete the file, in an interactive session. But just doing the first point is probably enough.

Inspired by #435

title: Thoughts about talking about reprexes
description:
I would like to share some thoughts on reprexes. I do not have any specific requests for code or documentation changes in the `reprex` package itself, but I would like to post this thread in case the maintainers find it useful.

I regularly find myself in a situation common to package maintainers: a user loosely describes an error and asks what might be the cause. Naturally, the error seems as strange to me as it does to the user, and I ask for a reprex. Sometimes the reprex is incomplete and not runnable, and other times the user does not provide one and instead requests that I speculate on a “likely” solution. As the discussion progresses, eventually they understand that as a package maintainer I do not have perfect knowledge. However, it is a lot of work to get there for each individual user. I find it hard to take a step back and explain the purpose of a reprex from first principles, and I find that I have to do this a lot.

I think the disconnect comes from an implicit difference of epistemology: the user insists on appealing to the expertise and authority of the maintainer, and the maintainer insists on extreme empiricism. So for [`targets`](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/), I wrote a [new chapter](https://books.ropensci.org/targets/help.html) in the user manual on how to ask for help, and I hope it bridges this and other gaps. From <https://books.ropensci.org/targets/help.html#post-the-complete-context>:

> Computer code is extremely strict. In order to run properly, it needs to be exactly correct, down to the last detail. That makes every single piece of every single computer program susceptible to programming errors and usage errors. For every bug you discover, there are hundreds of strange and unguessable potential causes. The culprit could be a typo buried deep in the targets codebase, an [incorrect hidden assumption lost in translation](https://youtu.be/2ve20PVNZ18?t=52) about how to use targets, an obscure bug in an obscure R package dependency, a mistake in one of your R functions, or some other mysterious or unexpected reason. In addition, you may be the first user to experience the problem. So when you ask for help, it is not enough to state the error and ask what might be the solution. The true answer is too surprising to predict, even for the most experienced experts of R and targets.
>
> To receive useful feedback, please provide the complete context of the problem, including a reprex. The purpose of a reprex, or reproducible example[1](https://books.ropensci.org/targets/help.html#fn1), is to eliminate the knowledge gaps, misunderstandings, and hidden assumptions where bugs hide. A reprex is a sample of complete, self-contained, runnable code that fully emulates and reproduces the problem. The code should [look clean and readable](https://style.tidyverse.org/), be as short and concise as possible, run in as few seconds as possible, and contain only the details most relevant to troubleshooting. You can embed the code inline in your question, or you can upload it to a public repository and post the link. Regardless, please expect that anyone trying to help will read all the code and run the enclosed _targets.R file on their own private computer. Please make this utterly empirical process as quick and easy as possible for the people who volunteer their valuable time and energy to answer questions.

title: Add wd panel to Rstudio Addins Menu
description:
Dear package maintainers,  I decided to create this issue since I would like to make a case for adding a new panel to the reprex_addin menu where a user can specify the `wd` for the reprex. 

In particular, I typically use the `reprex` package to create reproducible examples which also involve external files that must be read into the R session. Would you be interested in reviewing a PR?

title: Entrace base errors?
description:
This is a follow-up to #229 and how dev rlang always shows a backtrace on error in non-interactive sessions. It might be helpful and more consistent to entrace base errors with `rlang::entrace()`. Unfortunately, simply setting `options(error = rlang::entrace)` doesn't work because `rmarkdown::render()` captures the errors before `entrace()` has a chance to be called.

Would it be worth it to find a solution to that problem? The easiest way might be to add an option to entrace errors in rmarkdown itself.

title: Offer (or document) some "no theme" themes for RTF output
description:
Inspired by a recent chat with @DavisVaughan re: exerting a bit of control over highlighting for pasting into a talk

We already document how to use pre-existing themes:
https://reprex.tidyverse.org/articles/rtf.html#highlight-options

But sometimes that is not enough or too much.

In the "not enough" department, I have written up how to create and use a custom theme (also linked from the article):
https://github.com/jennybc/debugging/blob/master/how-to/highlight-custom-theme.md

But it might be nice to create a theme or at least document how to create and use some "no theme" themes, i.e. for when you're happy to apply colour in Keynote or whatever the destination software is.

You could imagine wanting a theme that's just "all black" or "all white" or "black (or white) code, grey output".

I think reprex could ship with themes and then that path could presumably be provided to the highlight. Requires a bit of experimentation.

title: BBCode support
description:
Hi,

I am using the reprex package frequently (thanks for this wonderful package) and mostly in a forum using BBCode.
I forked and added support to BBCode, but it's more of a hack than anything else (see `pp_md_to_bb()` function).

I wonder if there is a better way to support BBCode in reprex.
If not, I'll be happy to make a PR with the following chunks of codes (which only translate images and code blocks to BBCode).

* In `R/reprex_render.R` 
    ``` r
    pp_md_to_bb <- function(input) {
      bbout_file <- bb_file(input)
      output_lines <- read_lines(md_file(input))
      output_lines[grep("^``` r$", output_lines)] <- "[code=php]" # php is to add syntax coloration in legacy BBCode forum, before they added R
      output_lines[grep("^```$", output_lines)] <- "[/code]"
      output_lines <- gsub("^!\\[\\]\\((.+)\\)$", "[img]\\1[/img]", output_lines)
      write_lines(output_lines, bbout_file)
      bbout_file
    }
    ```
    With the following in `reprex_render_impl()`
    ``` r
      if (venue == "bb") {
        reprex_file <- pp_md_to_bb(input)
      }
    ```

* In `R/venues.R`
    ``` r
    #' @export
    #' @rdname reprex_venue
    reprex_bb <- function(...) reprex(..., venue = "bb")
    ```

* In `R/utils-io.R`
    ``` r
    bb_file <- function(path) {
      path_mutate(path, suffix = "reprex", ext = "txt")
    }
    ```

Best regards,
Mickaël

title: Prevent prex from changing certain session options
description:
Now, first, remember that `prex()` is unexported *precisely because* it creates leakage between your current R session and your (re)prex. So in general, `prex()` users have to take the bad with the good.

But we could try harder to leave certain things the way we found them.

Consider these options, which we inject into to-be-(re)prexed code:

https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/blob/318363cf7a911010ebb1593765cc21ec207d2d10/R/reprex_document.R#L131-L141

`prex()` could note the original values of `keep.source`, `rlang_backtrace_on_error_report`, and `crayon.enabled` and make a point of scheduling their restoration.

title: Reconsider using `rmarkdown::md_document("gfm")` or `rmarkdown::github_document()`
description:
This came up recently in #375 and #383 where @cderv points out that reprex would not benefit from a fix for this in rmarkdown itself, because `reprex_document()` isn't making direct use of rmarkdown's explicit functionality for preparing markdown for GitHub.

Historically, I know I had a good reason for this, however it's not at all clear if that still holds. Vaguely, it feels like rmarkdown went through a long phase where `github_document()` was not, actually, the best / most modern way to prepare markdown for GitHub. I think that's why I started using `md_document()` in the first place here in reprex. But the world has changed since then.

Philosophically, I'd love reprex to have ZERO knowledge of Pandoc minutiae and leave that for those maintaining rmarkdown. That is why I don't love this fix 293225e38424cbaaf672e5ef018c3891596ef369, but I'm taking it for now.

title: Parse error when braces are on a separate line
description:
When braces are on a separate line (see the `suppressWarnings()` difference where braces are on the same line vs. different lines at the top), reprex can generate a parse error:

The first example fails to parse with the error:

```
i Rendering reprex...
Error in parse(text = x, keep.source = TRUE) : 
  <text>:11:3: unexpected symbol
10:   rlang::warn("show this")
11:   rlang
      ^
```

```r
reprex::reprex({
rlang::warn("show this")
rlang::warn("hide this", class="hider")

suppressWarnings(
{
  rlang::warn("show this")
  rlang::warn("hide this", class="hider")
},
classes="hider")
})
```

The second example where the { is on the same line as `suppressWarnings(` succeeds:

``` r
rlang::warn("show this")
#> Warning: show this
rlang::warn("hide this", class="hider")
#> Warning: hide this

suppressWarnings({
  rlang::warn("show this")
  rlang::warn("hide this", class="hider")
},
classes="hider")
#> Warning: show this

Should reprex output add new lines with long (wide) error & warning messages?
description: When a reprex output shows a long warning or error message, it does not add new lines consistent with typical experience with character max-widths from the R console. For example, (perhaps an odd example, but it's one I recently used on RStudio Community) ```r library(dplyr) df <- tibble( y = LETTERS[1:3], x1 = 1:3, x2 = 3:5 ) lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = df) ``` this produces a somewhat long error, ``` r #> Warning in storage.mode(v) <- "double": NAs introduced by coercion #> Error in lm.fit(x, y, offset = offset, singular.ok = singular.ok, ...): NA/NaN/Inf in 'y' ``` In the console, this appears as the following, **Screenshot R Console:** On Stack Overflow, this appears as the following (not you have to scroll left to see the full error) **Screenshot Stack Overflow:** **Screenshot RStudio Community:** That horizontal scrolling can be awkward for some folks. Particularly for long errors and warnings (e.g. some package install errors). I feel it'd be ideal for warning and error messages to roughly replicate the new lines seen in the R console. New lines can certainly be added manually -- I have a feeling there are other concerns or trickiness I'm missing -- but I feel the default behavior should be with styling that works better on gh, so, and rstudio community.

title: Special considerations around base pipe `|>` and its placeholder `_`
description:
The introduction of the `_` placeholder for the base pipe `|>` is likely to result in lots of reports of `reprex()` not capturing folks reprex or error.

Because invalid use of `_` is going to result in a parse error, which is not something reprex can currently capture, because such code cannot be `rmarkdown::render()`ed.

@jthomasmock just shared these concrete examples with me.

In the Console, with R 4.2, one sees:

``` r
mtcars$disp |> mean
#> Error: The pipe operator requires a function call as RHS
```

or

``` r
mtcars$disp |> mean(_)
#> Error: pipe placeholder can only be used as a named argument
```

But an attempt to `reprex()` the expression `mtcars$disp |> mean(_)` results in:

``` r
ℹ Rendering reprex...
Error in parse(text = x, keep.source = TRUE) : 
  pipe placeholder can only be used as a named argument
```

This is really not a new phenomenon, i.e. we've long had users reporting similar situations where knitr's handling of parsing errors means the code can't be `reprex()`ed (e.g. #308, #359, #396). But I suspect increased use of `|>` means more people will bump up against this.

Hi,

Let me start by saying the reprex package is AWESOME and I use it on a daily basis as an RStudio Community Forum sustainer!

Now for the issue: I'm getting an error when running `reprex(venue="rtf")` . I did install the `highlight`  package successfully on my Windows 10 machine and was able to run it from command line. However, when trying to use it in the reprex function I get the following error

**ISSUE**
```
i Rendering reprex...
highlight: Output path equals input path: "C:/Users/PJ".
Error in `reprex_highlight()`:
! `highlight` call unsuccessful.
Backtrace:
    x
 1. \-reprex::reprex(...)
 2.   \-reprex:::reprex_impl(...)
 3.     \-reprex:::reprex_render_impl(...)
 4.       \-reprex:::pp_highlight(pp_md_to_r(md_file, comment = comment))
 5.         \-reprex:::reprex_highlight(r_file_rendered(input), rtf_file)
 6.           \-rlang::abort("`highlight` call unsuccessful.")
Warning message:
In shell(cmd) :
  'highlight  -i C:/Users/PJ Van Camp/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpqEtOYh/reprex-32e06047533c-stuck-crane/stuck-crane_reprex_r.R --out-format=rtf --no-trailing-nl --encoding=UTF-8 --style darkbone --font "Courier Regular" --font-size 50  -o C:/Users/PJ Van Camp/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpqEtOYh/reprex-32e06047533c-stuck-crane/stuck-crane_reprex_r.rtf' execution failed with error code 1
```

I figured out that the reason for this error is that my home folder unfortunately has spaces in it ` C:/Users/PJ Van Camp/` and the highlight tool is cutting the path after the first space producing the above error.

**PROPOSED SOLUTION**
In the source code when calling the highlight tool, make sure to quote the input and output path and all should be solved. I tried this running the actual command reported in the error with proper quotes like this ...
```
highlight  -i "C:/Users/PJ Van Camp/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpqEtOYh/reprex-32e06047533c-stuck-crane/stuck-crane_reprex_r.R" \
--out-format=rtf --no-trailing-nl --encoding=UTF-8 --style darkbone --font "Courier Regular" --font-size 50  \
-o "C:/Users/PJ Van Camp/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpqEtOYh/reprex-32e06047533c-stuck-crane/stuck-crane_reprex_r.rtf"
```
... and the correct file was generated without error!

I hope you could implement this so I (and other Windows users with spaces in their path names) could use the   rtf functionality in reprex.

Thanks!
PJ

title: Feature request:  include `rgl` output automatically.
description:
It would be nice if `rgl` output was automatically included in `reprex()` output.  This should be easy to do because `knitr` has supported `rgl` output for a while now.  All that is needed is to run `rgl::setupKnitr(autoprint = TRUE)` and snapshots of output will be produced.  

To set this automatically, `reprex()` could run the following code:

```
setHook(packageEvent("rgl", "onLoad"),
        function(...) rgl::setupKnitr(autoprint = TRUE))
```

I would be happy to submit a PR to do this if you give me a hint where it should happen.  Here's what output would look like with this addition (though of course the`setHook()` call won't be displayed if `reprex()` runs it internally):
``` r
setHook(packageEvent("rgl", "onLoad"),
        function(...) rgl::setupKnitr(autoprint = TRUE))
library(rgl)
plot3d(1:10, 1:10, 1:10)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/8K31bUM.png)

<sup>Created on 2022-01-23 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

For anyone reading this and running `reprex` without this facility, you don't really need to do it as a hook, it's enough to run the line in the code you're reproducing, e.g.

```
rgl::setupKnitr(autoprint = TRUE))
library(rgl)
plot3d(1:10, 1:10, 1:10)
```

title: Move `master` branch to `main`

The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

title: Default to ragg graphics device if available for rendering
description:
I was recently trying to make a reprex that used custom fonts and I couldn't figure out a way to specify the graphic device used for rendering the reprex. Because of this (on my Windows machine) I wasn't able to use a custom font in my ggplot reprex. Since ragg/systemfonts seems to work quite well across all OS, would it make sense to set ragg as the default graphics device for the R Markdown's rendered by reprex?

Recently, [`ggplot2::ggsave()` made ragg the default device](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/pull/4388) if it is installed.

``` r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, cyl)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Jokerman")

title: Pandoc versions 2.13+ include the yaml header in the output for GFM
description:
With pandoc 2.12 this works as expected.

``` r
tmp <- fs::dir_create(fs::file_temp())
reprex::reprex(input = "rmarkdown::pandoc_version()\n", venue = "gh", wd = tmp, advertise = FALSE)
readLines(fs::dir_ls(tmp, glob = "*md"))
#> [1] "``` r"                       "rmarkdown::pandoc_version()"
#> [3] "#> [1] '2.12'"               "```"
```

With pandoc 2.13 we get the YAML header as well

``` r
tmp <- fs::dir_create(fs::file_temp())
reprex::reprex(input = "rmarkdown::pandoc_version()\n", venue = "gh", wd = tmp, advertise = FALSE)
readLines(fs::dir_ls(tmp, glob = "*md"))
#>  [1] "---"                          "author: jhester"             
#>  [3] "date: 2021-04-28"             "output:"                     
#>  [5] "  reprex::reprex_document:"   "    advertise: false"        
#>  [7] "title: legal-mink\\_reprex.R" "---"                         
#>  [9] ""                             "``` r"                       
#> [11] "rmarkdown::pandoc_version()"  "#> [1] '2.13'"               
#> [13] "```"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-04-28 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

It looks like this is fallout from https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/6537, pandoc now parses the YAML header for GFM, before it was silently discarded.

I think likely reprex will have to either remove the header from the input file it sends to pandoc, or remove it from the output after the fact.

title: Feature request: overload library() to print user's package version
description:
When users post a reprex, an immediate question is often "what version are you using of package X"? For this reason, I often post my reprexes starting with `packageVersion()` calls.

This line of questioning can be eliminated altogether by running the reprex in an environment where `library()` and `require()` have been overwritten with something simple, such as:

``` r
library <- function(x) {
    x <- as.character(substitute(x))
    message(x, " version ", packageVersion(x))
    base::library(x, character.only = TRUE)
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(dplyr)
    library(plotly)
})
#> dplyr version 1.0.5
#> plotly version 4.9.3

# showing the packages are actually loaded
data.frame(a = 1) %>% mutate(b = 2)
#>   a b
#> 1 1 2
```

title: Reprex not rendering every gganimate animation
description:
Hello,

When trying to render a reprex containing multiple gganimate animations, I found that reprex would only produce the final animation so I had to do each one separately and manually stitch them together afterwards. See https://github.com/thomasp85/gganimate/issues/438 specifically but I'll do a simpler version here, only the second animation, `anim2`, will be produced by reprex::reprex() below...

``` r
library(gganimate)
#> Loading required package: ggplot2

data <- tibble::tibble(dates = seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2022-12-31"), by = 1),
                       x = rep(seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2021-12-31"), by = 1), 2),
                       y = as.numeric(1:730),
                       type = c(rep("A", 365), rep("B", 365)))

# notice colours of lines start wrong and flicker
p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = type, group = type)) +
  geom_path()

anim <- p +
  transition_reveal(dates)
anim

# similar but more pronounced when manually specifying colours - not even a solid line at first
p2 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = type, group = type)) +
  geom_path() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey", "red"))

anim2 <- p2 +
  transition_reveal(dates)
anim2
```

When sharing code on reddit (e.g., on the nice [r/rstats](https://www.reddit.com/r/rstats/) subreddit) code blocks _can_ be formatted in two ways: fences or indentation. Both methods are also supported by GFM. However, only indentation is backwards compatible with the still-popular older reddit UI (https://old.reddit.com/).

Per the [reddit markdown wiki](https://www.reddit.com/wiki/markdown#wiki_code_blocks_and_inline_code):

> 🔮 New Reddit note: Indented code blocks are the only form of code block that works on Old Reddit. Use them for compatibility.

See [this comment thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/rstats/comments/ly9zs7/data_frame_class_and_levels/gpsf589?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web2x&context=3) for an example of this issue when using reprex.

title: accommodate renv projects with reprex?
description:
From https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/208.

Projects using `renv` typically require some extra gymnastics, which are performed (normally) through the use of a project `.Rprofile`. However, `reprex()` does not read that `.Rprofile` by default, leading to some subtle differences in how `reprex()` runs code versus how `renv` might run that same code.

It could be worth considering whether `reprex()` could support this by default; e.g. by allowing the project `.Rprofile` to be loaded -- either by default, or when it detects or knows `renv` is active.

title: Contemplate callr:r()'s user_profile argument
description:
The default behaviour for the `user_profile` argument  has changed since reprex last got serious attention: 

```
3.4.0 (2019-12-09) system_profile = FALSE, user_profile = "project",
2.0.0 (2018-01-28) system_profile = FALSE, user_profile = FALSE,      <-- I think my use of callr is designed for this
1.0.0 (2016-06-18) system_profile = TRUE, user_profile = TRUE,
```

Documentation for the argument:

> Whether to use the user's profile file. If this is "project", then only the profile from the working directory is used, but the R_PROFILE_USER environment variable and the user level profile are not.

In normal usage, I think it's OK that reprex is ignorant of `user_profile` because by default we reprex in the temp dir and, therefore, no `.Rprofile` is used by `callr::r()`.

But if `outfile` is used, a project-level `.Rprofile` is potentially used. At the very least, this feels like something to be analyzed and documented. It's conceivable I should set `user_profile = FALSE` in reprex (that would be the most conservative approach in terms of not allowing changes in callr to change behaviour of reprex https://github.com/r-lib/callr/pull/135#issuecomment-559907943).

title: Better handling for shinyApps
description:
Currently:

```
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("n", "N", 1:10),
  plotOutput("plot")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    n <- input$n * 2
    plot(head(cars, n))
  })
}
shinyApp(server, ui)
#> 
#> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:8630
#> Warning: Error in <-: argument "output" is missing, with no default
#> Warning: Error in ui: argument "output" is missing, with no default
....
#> Warning: Error in ui: argument "output" is missing, with no default
#> Warning in normalizePath(f): path[1]="webshot316228a29709.png": No such
#> file or directory
#> Warning in file(con, "rb"): cannot open file 'webshot316228a29709.png': No
#> such file or directory
#> Error in file(con, "rb"): cannot open the connection
```

And it requires frantic hammering of escape to stop it running.

While we could use shinytest to create a screenshot, I think the best option is probably to set some option so that shiny doesn't try and run the app in the first place. This is more about avoiding a currently annoying behaviour than making reprex a great tool for reprexing shiny apps.

title: Switch to shiny based alert for error
description:
My console is on the top right side of my RStudio. 

When I launch the reprex addin and have a `{yesno}` question, I always miss the question, as the addin hides the console:

![Screenshot 2019-07-16 at 11 09 46](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17936236/61281632-3ff09d80-a7ba-11e9-9151-5814a53531e4.png)

So in this case I always stare at my screen for a couple of seconds before realising that something has happened in my console, and I have to move around my addin to see: 

![Screenshot 2019-07-16 at 11 10 36](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17936236/61281690-5d256c00-a7ba-11e9-83b3-0f3263672a89.png)

And once I've done that, the console waits for me to enter something, but I can't as the addin is blocking me from accessing the console. 

If I click on "Cancel", nothing happens. If I click on "Render", nothing happens. Both these buttons are designed to execute R code, but the console is waiting for an input.  I have to click on the cross to close the addin and enter things in the console. 

I feel switching to a shiny-based alert system (which would be quite straightforward to implement in JS) would be a better user-experience for these kinds of cases.

title: argument or option to automatically open file that holds rendered reprex
description:
Please briefly describe your problem and what output you expect. If
you have a question, please don't use this form. Instead, ask on
<https://community.rstudio.com/> or <https://stackoverflow.com/>.

---

Brief description of the problem

When I create a reprex on rstudio.cloud, I am always reminded that the reprex package cannot save my markdown for me in the clipboard and I am prompted to answer a question about opening the output file for manual copy:

```r
library(reprex)
reprex(y <- x)
#> Rendering reprex...
#> Clipboard on X11 requires 'xclip' (recommended) or 'xsel'.
#> Unable to put result on the clipboard. How to get it:
#>   * Capture what `reprex()` returns.
#>   * Consult the output file. Control via `outfile` argument.
#> Path to `outfile`:
#>   * /tmp/RtmpiFZNg0/reprexc323d3fbd9/reprex_reprex.md
#> Open the output file for manual copy?
#> 1: yes
#> 2: no
#> 
#> Selection: 1
```

I would like to bypass the yes/no question asking if i want to open the output file for manual copy, by setting a function option. In the example below, I propose a new logical function option, named `show_markdown`, that will:
1. automatically open the output file for manual copy when set to TRUE
2. skip opening the output file for manual copy when set to FALSE
3. prompt the user to open the output file for manual copy when set to NULL, NA, or any non-logical type.

Scenario 1: automatically open the output file for manual copy
```r
library(reprex)
reprex(y <- x, show_markdown=TRUE)
#> Rendering reprex...
#> Clipboard on X11 requires 'xclip' (recommended) or 'xsel'.
#> Unable to put result on the clipboard. How to get it:
#>   * Capture what `reprex()` returns.
#>   * Consult the output file. Control via `outfile` argument.
#> Path to `outfile`:
#>   * /tmp/RtmpiFZNg0/reprexc323d3fbd9/reprex_reprex.md
```
Window with markdown should be displayed to user.

Scenario 2: skip opening the output file for manual copy
```r
library(reprex)
reprex(y <- x, show_markdown=FALSE)
#> Rendering reprex...
#> Clipboard on X11 requires 'xclip' (recommended) or 'xsel'.
#> Unable to put result on the clipboard. How to get it:
#>   * Capture what `reprex()` returns.
#>   * Consult the output file. Control via `outfile` argument.
#> Path to `outfile`:
#>   * /tmp/RtmpiFZNg0/reprexc323d3fbd9/reprex_reprex.md
```
Window with markdown should not be displayed to user. Probably most useful when combined with setting the `outfile` option so the name of the output file is predictable.

Scenario 3: (default scenario) prompt the user to open the output file for manual copy
```r
library(reprex)
reprex(y <- x, show_markdown=NULL)
#> Rendering reprex...
#> Clipboard on X11 requires 'xclip' (recommended) or 'xsel'.
#> Unable to put result on the clipboard. How to get it:
#>   * Capture what `reprex()` returns.
#>   * Consult the output file. Control via `outfile` argument.
#> Path to `outfile`:
#>   * /tmp/RtmpiFZNg0/reprexc323d3fbd9/reprex_reprex.md
#> Open the output file for manual copy?
#> 1: yes
#> 2: no
#> 
#> Selection: 1
```
User will select 1 or 2 to determine whether a window with markdown should not be displayed.

})

title: Feature request: venue = "piazza"
description:
I'd love to have more students using reprex when asking questions on Piazza, and I think there may be two challenges with it that the reprex package could potentially address. The biggest challenge, of course, is making a reprex, but that's on me to teach. Note that I'm primarily focusing on intro students who are learning R via R Markdown documents.

Currently, `venue = "gh"` works on Piazza out of the box, and it's what I use when I respond to student questions. However, I think the following could help student adoption:

1. Offer `venue = "piazza"`, even if it's just an alias to `venue = "gh"`: There are two reasons for this: (1) it might help buy-in and (2) it might help reduce confusion in a course where we're using GitHub as well but not for the purpose of general Q&A and there are already too many tool names to keep track of that it would be nice to not have to say "to post on Piazza use the GitHub venue for your reprex".

2. `venue = "gh"` works but `venue = "piazza"` could be formatted to be more aligned with R Markdown and more robust to student error:

Suppose I have the following code that I want to reprex:

```r
x <- 2
x * 2
plot(cars)
```

If I run this through `venue = "gh"` I get the following

```
    x <- 2
    x * 2
    #> [1] 4
    plot(cars)

![](https://i.imgur.com/BKttr08.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-10-05 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>
```

which works both on GitHub and on Piazza. However, it requires that (1) there is a line break between this and any potential text above it (2) that students understand that indented text will be formatted as code. I'm finding both of these challenging with my students. A slightly modified output that would also work on Piazza is as follows (but imagine there isn't a space between the first and the second ` in):

```
` ``
x <- 2
x * 2
#> [1] 4
plot(cars)
` ``
![](https://i.imgur.com/J99dF3Z.png)

<sup>Created on 2020-10-05 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>
```

Having explicit fences makes it robust to (1) above (code formatting works with and without a space between text and code) and, I think, also addresses (2) where students learn in Rmd documents that "code goes in chunks".

I'm wondering if supporting this sounds reasonable for reprex, and if so, if you'd prefer a PR.

title: Tidyr pivot_longer and pivot_longer_spec feature request
description:
Specific feature request: please enable pivot_longer's values_ptypes argument to handle exceptional cases whereby the input columns used to generate the variables generated from values_to are not of the same type.

```r
dataframe %>% 
      # drop nonsensical columns that are completely empty
      select(
        -matches("x\\d+|v\\d+")
      ) %>% 
      # If a variable's measurement number is not given (i.e. variable name 
      # does not have pattern "_\\d+$"), then assume that, for that variable,
      # one and only one measurement is taken, and it is the first.
      rename_at(
        vars(matches("_C\\d+$")),
        ~paste0(., "_1")
      ) %>% 
      pivot_longer(
        cols = matches("_\\d+$"),
        names_to = c(".value", "event_name_multiple_events", "CRF version", "reading"),
        names_pattern = "(.*)_(E\\d_\\d)_(C\\d+)_(\\d+$)",
        values_ptypes = list(ics_laba = character()),
        values_drop_na = TRUE
      )
# Code breaks at pivot_longer because some input columns of the dataframe that are used to #generate one of the values_to variables are not of the same type. Should include a scalable #exception handler in this case.
```

title: `venue = roxygen`?
description:
I'd like to propose another option for `venue`: roxygen.

This feature would make writing `@examples` a bit easier. In particular it would avoid having to prefix the code with `#'` for the code part and `#' #>` for the output, reduce accidental commits of syntactically (or otherwise) incorrect examples, and make it easier to identify dependencies.

On the last point, it may be appropriate to assume that when `venue = 'rox'` and one is working within a package directory that the package source in the current directory is attached. (So that `library(<mypackage>)` is not necessary in the rendered output.)

I can make a PR if you'd like. I searched for roxygen in the issues list but only found references to current behaviour, not feature requests refused.

title: differences between `reprex_addin()` vs `reprex()` on Wayland

title: Change the default for `std_out_err` to allow seeing the stderr
description:
Feel free to open a new issue about whether to change the default for `std_out_err` and/or to put it under the control of an option. I'm hesitant to turn it on by default, because now we're vulnerable to any glitches in how that works in callr. So I lean towards: keep the default as `FALSE` but make it possible for people who frequently reprex with packages where they need `std_out_err` to set a personal default of `TRUE`.

_Originally posted by @jennybc in https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/issues/278#issuecomment-517815558_

title: Workaround needed to render bash shell code when reporting R issue
description:
Sometimes, I need to create a reproducible R code from bash shell when reporting issues.
I was wondering if there would be any way to render `bash` scripts in `reprex::reprex()`. I was attempting to render the following code using `rmarkdown::github_document` alternatively; however, it fails when error occurs while rendering bash scripts.
In sum, I think we need a way to make a reproducible bash code including its error messages for reporting issue.
Below is an example bash code I was attempting to report to `xaringan` package including its error message; however, I could not find any way to do. Thus, I just had to report its input code without any output message.

```{bash}
# Creating a sample template Rmd file:
Rscript --vanilla -e "rmarkdown::draft('resume.Rmd', 'html-resume', 'pagedown', create_dir = FALSE, edit = FALSE)"

# Render the sample Rmd file using shell:
Rscript --vanilla -e "xaringan::infinite_moon_reader('resume.Rmd')"
```

title: Venue as suffix
description:
I find myself doing `reprex(venue = "R")` fairly often, usually for Slack, and I find it aggravating.

Seriously considering having suffix-y forms to specify venue. Something like so:

``` r
reprex_r <- function(...) reprex(..., venue = "R")
reprex_rtf <- function(...) reprex(..., venue = "rtf")
# and so on
```

Would need to think about how this interacts with my keyboard shortcut, but that's more of a personal matter. Shortcut could be rewired to lead to a quick choice of venue, probably console-based.

cc @hadley

title: Record known limitation re: reprexing in a directory with rmarkdown-controlling YAML
description:
If you try to reprex with `outfile = NA` or `outfile = some_local_file` with working directory in an R Markdown website, you will fail. That's because `rmarkdown::render()` honors the YAML found in `_site.yml` and this overrides the output format requested in the YAML of the `.R` file that reprex creates. The reprex might be rendered to, say, html, instead of the intended markdown.

If this came up a lot, I might do something about it, but it really doesn't.

Solutions:

Just call `reprex()` with a different working directory. E.g., use another an RStudio instance that's open to some other kind of Project, i.e. a package or anything that lacks global rmarkdown YAML config.

You can even use withr if you want to `reprex()` from inside an R Markdown website, with a different working directory for the duration of the call:

``` r
withr::with_dir(
  "~/tmp",
  reprex(1:3, outfile = NA)
)
```

title: suggestion: data obscurator
description:
For discussion: what are your thoughts on the value of an "obscuration" function? Frequently I see (and have experienced as an asker) the pain of questions that cannot show actual data, whether due to PII/HIPPA, IP, company rules, etc. Occasionally the asker will be savvy enough to concoct some fake data, either programmatically or by other means. Those without the skills, however, are left asking unsubstantiated questions (fielding requests for reproducibility, perhaps being closed for "no data, no code").

"Anonymizing" the data (similar to survey data) is not always sufficient, since the numbers or categories themselves might be indicative of the type of data (if hiding that is important to the asker). Hashing/ciphering the text is also not good, as patterns might develop. The point is to be irreversible.

I suggest some simple (and at times, ugly) functions that would turn something like:

```r
indata
# # A tibble: 2 x 7
#   ssn         lname address               phone        lgl     int   num
#   <chr>       <chr> <chr>                 <chr>        <lgl> <dbl> <dbl>
# 1 123-45-6789 Smith 123 Main St           504-586-1928 TRUE     73  3.14
# 2 234-56-7890 Doe   1600 Pennsylvania Ave 201-293-2222 FALSE     2 -2.72
obscure(indata)
# # A tibble: 2 x 7
#   ssn         lname address          phone        lgl     int   num
#   <chr>       <chr> <chr>            <chr>        <lgl> <dbl> <dbl>

The individual filters can be smarter in order to keep some patterns ... perhaps looking for U.S. SSNs and several patterns of US and international phone numbers, but I don't think much effort is strictly needed here.

I'd think `reprex` is a great place for functionality like this: as the use of it (for me, mostly seen on SO) grows, it is becoming easier to suggest to new users "use `reprex` to improve this question"; even better if problems with data privacy can be addressed in the same place.

title: reprex() does not copy and paste output into clipboard when render argument is set to FALSE.
description:
Please briefly describe your problem and what output you expect. If
you have a question, please don't use this form. Instead, ask on
<https://community.rstudio.com/> or <https://stackoverflow.com/>.

---

Brief description of the problem

`reprex()` function does not copy and paste any output into clipboard when `render=F` is set.
The function utilizes clipboard only when the render option is set to TRUE; however, for those who use batch files and do not necessarily need to check rendered output should turn off the option while still being able to get the copied output text on their clipboard.

``` r
reprex::reprex("print(1:5)", render=F)
```

title: Include time reprex took to run with information in italics at the bottom
Reprex with asynchronous functions
description:
First of all, thanks for the **reprex** package, I love it!

It seems that making a reprex with asynchronous functions built on top of the [**later**](https://cran.r-project.org/package=later) package is not yet possible. AFAIK, this is not surprising. 
Even if this issue is related to other packages, I fill an issue here to document the consequences on the **reprex** package.

Here are two examples.

#### With the **promises** package
Take this reprex:

``` r
library(promises)
promise_reject("Dummy message")
#> <Promise [rejected: simpleError]>
```

<sup>Created on 2019-05-06 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

The expected result is:

``` r
library(promises)
promise_reject("Dummy message")
#> <Promise [rejected: simpleError]>
#> Unhandled promise error: Dummy message
```

#### With the later package

``` r
library(later)
later(~ message("Dummy message"), delay = 0)
```

<sup>Created on 2019-05-06 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

The expected result is:

``` r
library(later)
later(~ message("Dummy message"), delay = 0)
#> Dummy message
```

#### Related issues
- https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1560 
- https://github.com/rstudio/promises/issues/26

title: `utils::file.edit()` silently fails in `reprex()` when `reprex()` is run in an RStudio session on Windows
description:
* Issue related to line https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/blob/8c64e133ac7050bad02151cfb511c138e0a6c30d/R/reprex.R#L377

* This issue may have gone unnoticed thus far b/c `utils::file.edit()` is wrapped in `defer()` and `defer()` seems to muffle errors (CC'ing @kevinushey, as I'm not sure if this is desired behavior):

``` r
library(withr)
fo <- function() {
  defer({
    print("printing")
    stop("stoping")
  })
}
fo()
#> [1] "printing"
```

Created on 2018-09-13 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.0.9000).

* If `reprex()` didn't wrap `utils::file.edit()` in `defer()`, the user would see the following error to explain why no file had been opened: 

```r
some_file <- tempfile()
utils::file.edit(some_file)
#> Error in editor(file = file, title = title) : 
#>  argument "name" is missing, with no default
```

I believe this error stems from the fact that RStudio sets the "editor" option to be the following function on Windows:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/blob/8af730409bb6d651cc8f6816d136bea91441e7a4/src/cpp/session/modules/SessionEnvironment.R#L379

.. but this function doesn't seem to play well with `utils::file.edit()` (it does work with RStudio's `file.edit()` though).

* Relevant info on the platform on which `reprex()` fails to open file:

R version: 3.4.4 (2018-03-15)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 7 x64 (build 7601) Service Pack 1
RStudio version: 1.1.419

* PR on the way

title: checking for non-deterministic output
description:
I noticed a [reprex-created chunk on SO](https://stackoverflow.com/q/55148371) and was surprised that it was not reproducible -- `rbinom` is used but there's no `set.seed` before it.

A crude pseudo fix would be to have reprex compile its output twice and test equality, warning the user on failure.

Omitting `set.seed` seems like a pretty common user error when it comes to making reprexes and it would be nice to catch, so hopefully addressing it is in scope. I noticed that no-repro-because-local-file is out of scope https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/issues/191#issuecomment-389348964 but I guess the fix there is a lot tougher (...run the code in a virtual machine or something).

title: Feature request: venue = "html"
description:
A few places I would like to post reprexes, most notably the LMS [canvas](https://canvas.instructure.com/), won't accept markdown, but will allow HTML input. I propose an additional `venue = "html"` that would render using `output: html_fragment`. So, for example the code: ```r reprex({ (y <- 1:4) mean(y) }, venue = "html") ``` would place the following on the clipboard: ```html 
(y <- 1:4)
#> [1] 1 2 3 4
mean(y)
#> [1] 2.5
``` This can be pasted into the "HTML Editor" in canvas: Which canvas renders into something like: I have an attempt implementing this which only involves an additional file to `make_filenames()` and an additional condition in `reprex()`. Would you accept a PR for this? Any thoughts on any lurking gotchas with this venue?

title: Submit update to CRAN
Prevent `reprex()` from successfully running if it is not a reprex
description:
Thought inspired by [conversation on this thread](https://community.rstudio.com/t/faq-whats-a-reproducible-example-reprex-and-how-do-i-do-one/5219/13).

The purpose of the package `reprex` seems a little unclear to me:

- is it to render code for sharing (as suggested by the main package description: "Render bits of R code for sharing")?
- is it to render reprexes for sharing (as suggested by the package name and the sentence: "What is a reprex? It’s a reproducible example, as coined by Romain Francois.")?

Since `reprex` does more than just rendering bits of R code (it also runs that code in a fresh environment and gives helpful error messages if the code is not a reprex) and with such a name, I think the intent is more likely to be the later.

If the purpose is to produce nicely formatted reprexes, I wonder whether it is a good idea to have `reprex()` output nicely formatted reprex-looking chunks that are not reprexes when run on non-reprexes. Admittedly, those do have an error message. But that message seems to be ignored by some new R users who think that they are posting reprexes, for instance on the [RStudio Community site](https://community.rstudio.com/).

This also has the effect of blurring the concept of reprex with the idea of formatted code.

The tidyverse functions are often more strict than their base R counterparts: they will not run but will give an error message when there are data type inconsistencies for instance (while the base R functions would give an output, for better or for worse). I really like this behaviour. I like the idea of functions not running if fed inadequate code. I was wondering if having `reprex()` *only* output the error message (and not a reprex-looking chunk) when run on a non-reprex might not make the package more inline with this philosophy as well as making the actual concept of reprex much more clear to new R users?

Then one could safely say "`reprex()` outputs a reprex", which is not always the case now. And asking people to use the package `reprex` would necessarily mean to make a reprex in the first place (since without a reprex, the code would not run but just give an error message). People would never post what they think is a reprex when it isn't. It might make helping them easier, but mostly, it might be more pedagogical about the actual concept of reprex (which seems to be surrounded by a fair amount of confusion amongst people new to R).

title: Enable package management reminders/best practice
description:
Is there any good reason why the pacman package is not used in tandem with reprex? I can understand why the need to be explicit with loading is good to see what exactly the messages are are startup, but it can be bothersome to write out 6 or more `library` or `require` calls to simply load packages for a `reprex`. In my experience creating reprex's, I have found that while it is useful to explicitly state the packages loaded for a given example, I think it would save much amount of code to utilize existing functions so that you can easily load up libraries as such, and easily unload. Below is an example where I had a hard time finding base code to load and unload an r package in one script, yet the `pacman::p_unload(dplyr)` was incredibly useful to make a very succinct script.

Related issue on package messages not appearing in `pacman`:
https://github.com/trinker/pacman/issues/99

One side note is that while it looks that dplyr has an odd character �, the reprex rendered HTML is OK:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7308115/30840431-d93710ee-a23c-11e7-8d67-abb239fd6bb0.png)


``` r
##########################

data_t_five <- structure(c(0L, 2L, 3L, 9L, 8L, 0L, 0L, 14L, 0L, 3L, 1L, 3L, 
                           0L, 9L, 3L, 3L, 10L, 13L, 14L, 14L, 1L, 5L, 8L, 10L, 12L, 0L, 
                           1L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 5L, 10L, 13L, 15L, 14L, 0L, 0L, 3L, 8L, 2L, 0L, 
                           1L, 6L, 3L, 7L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 12L, 0L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 5L, 0L, 
                           0L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 0L, 2L, 6L, 9L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 7L, 14L, 15L, 0L, 
                           0L, 2L, 15L, 3L, 0L, 6L, 6L, 10L, 14L, 3L, 1L, 6L, 13L, 15L, 
                           0L, 0L, 0L, 4L, 3L, 0L, 6L, 3L, 0L, 5L, 6L, 11L, 15L, 16L, 15L, 
                           1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 10L, 7L, 0L, 1L, 8L, 2L, 3L, 
                           0L, 0L, 1L, 0L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 3L), .Dim = c(5L, 25L), .Dimnames = list(
                             c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May"), NULL))
#library(tidyr)
#library(magrittr)
#library(tibble)
#library(dplyr)
pacman::p_load(tidyr, magrittr, tibble, dplyr)
first_five_mod = data.frame(data_t_five)
##Verify 'rownames' is a column name
f=first_five_mod %>%
  rownames_to_column %>% 
  gather(var, value, -rowname)
colnames(f)
#> [1] "rowname" "var"     "value"
##Try to filter df for rowname = "Jan" without explicit dplyr
##dplyr was not loaded so it tried to call filter from package stats, which threw
## an error
pacman::p_unload(dplyr)
#> The following packages have been unloaded:
#>  dplyr
f=first_five_mod %>%
  rownames_to_column %>% 
  gather(var, value, -rowname) %>%
  filter(rowname == "Jan")
#> Warning in data.matrix(data): NAs introduced by coercion

#> Warning in data.matrix(data): NAs introduced by coercion
#> Error in filter(., rowname == "Jan"): object 'rowname' not found

##Works using explicict dplyr call
f=first_five_mod %>%
  rownames_to_column %>% 
  gather(var, value, -rowname) %>%
  dplyr::filter(rowname == "Jan")

########################
```

title: Argument / option to apply re-style code with styler
description:
I'm switching from `formatR::tidy_source()` to [`styler::style_text()`](https://github.com/krlmlr/styler#readme) (#94). The most specific motivation is styler's ability to handle tidy eval code. Currently reprex re-styles code that came via expression, because the srcref approach mutilates leading whitespace.

Now that I'm playing with styler I wonder if reprex should re-style **all** code. At least by default? 

I could add an argument to control re-styling, that defaults to `TRUE`. BTW I have plans to make several arguments like this settable via an option, so they're easy to set in a startup file.

This would have the effect of putting good code style in front of the eyeballs of all reprex authors and consumers.

cc @hadley @jimhester

packageVersion("reprex")

packageVersion("reprex")

title: inline comments not always preserved
description:
with reprex 0.1.1, i noticed that the output does not contain all of the input comments.

running:
```r
reprex::reprex({
 a <- 1 #this is a comment
 b <- 2 #this is a second comment
},venue = "gh", outfile = "reprex")
```

produces:

``` r
a <- 1 #this is a comment
b <- 2                   
```

which contains one comment but not the other.  This seems to occur when there are no other commands following a comment as illustrated by:

```r
reprex::reprex({
 a <- 1 #this is a comment
 b <- 2 #this is a second comment
 c <- 3 #This is the third comment
},venue = "gh", outfile = "reprex")
```

``` r
a <- 1 #this is a comment       
b <- 2 #this is a second comment
c <- 3                          
```

title: Trailing text (prose) not rendered for expression input
description:
If a `reprex` ends with text, the text following the code is not rendered. I.e. this `reprex` code:

    reprex({
    #' If a `reprex` ends with text, the text following the code is not rendered
    x <- 1:2 
    #' Trailing text
    })

...generates this:

If a `reprex` ends with text, the text following the code is not rendered

``` r
x <- 1:2
```
-------

    reprex({
      #' Add some code after the trailing text to render it
      x <- 1:2
      #' Non-trailing text is rendered
      x
      })
Add some code after the trailing text to render it

``` r
x <- 1:2
```

Non-trailing text is rendered

``` r
x
#> [1] 1 2
```

title: Restyle expression-derived source with styler
description:
Expression input generally gets processed with `formatR::tidy_source()` due to the addition of this line in the `.R` source file:

```r
knitr::opts_chunk$set(tidy = TRUE, tidy.opts = list(indent = 2))
```

But this does not play well with the bang-bang syntactic sugar from tidyeval:

``` r
formatR::tidy_source(
  text = c(
    "nameshift <- c(SL = 'Sepal.Length')",
    "head(dplyr::rename(iris[,1:2], !!!nameshift), 3)"
  )
)
#> nameshift <- c(SL = "Sepal.Length")
#> head(dplyr::rename(iris[, 1:2], !(!(!nameshift))), 3)
```

[styler](https://github.com/krlmlr/styler#readme) is under development and its non-invasive quality works to our advantage:

``` r
styler::style_text(
  c(
    "nameshift <- c(SL = 'Sepal.Length')",
    "head(dplyr::rename(iris[,1:2], !!!nameshift), 3)"
  )
)
#> [1] "nameshift <- c(SL = \"Sepal.Length\")"            
#> [2] "head(dplyr::rename(iris[, 1:2], !!!nameshift), 3)"
```

Switch to that once it's on CRAN.

cc @krlmlr @lorenzwalthert

``` r

title: reprex_rescue does not handle continuation lines.
special characters in prompts need to be escaped before being used in a regex.
description:
I just changed my prompt to be a blue `>` with

```r
getOption("prompt")
#> [1] "\033[34m> \033[39m"
```

Which now gives the following output when you try to use reprex
```r
reprex::reprex(input = "x <- 1\n")
Error in grepl(regex, x) :
  invalid regular expression '^> ', reason 'Missing ']''
```

This is because https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex/blob/04fcbbc7784ae14cf4993e03b9a81ca8ee647833/R/ensure.R#L25-L26
Does not escape the prompt for special regex characters before passing it to `grepl()`.

Will have a PR to fix this shortly.

title: Allow user to specify variables to be included as dput
description:
One common thing users forget to do in a reproducible example is to share the variables they've already defined (for example, datasets they're working with). You can turn a variable into a reproducible chunk of code with `dput`.

If we already have a few variables defined, it would be good to be able to add them to the start of the reprex code automatically. Here's a hello-world version using lazy_eval:

``` r
define_vars <- function(...) {
  vs <- lazyeval::lazy_dots(...)

  varnames <- unname(sapply(vs, function(v) as.character(v$expr)))

  dputs <- sapply(vs, function(v) {
    v$expr <- substitute(capture.output(dput(x)), list(x = v$expr))
    lazyeval::lazy_eval(v)
  })

  paste(varnames, dputs, sep = " <- ")
}
```

This takes one or more variables as its arguments and turns them into code that defines those variables. For example:

``` r
a <- 1:5
d <- data.frame(a = 1:5, b = 2)

varcode <- define_vars(a, d)

# turns it into code
cat(varcode, sep = "\n")
#> a <- 1:5
#> d <- c("structure(list(a = 1:5, b = c(2, 2, 2, 2, 2)), .Names = c(\"a\", ", "\"b\"), row.names = c(NA, -5L), class = \"data.frame\")")
```

In the end version of reprex, I imagine having a `vars` function, which creates an argument suitable for passing in:

``` r
y <- 1:100
reprex({y + 2}, vars = vars(y))
# even though it wasn't included in the reprex, resulting code would start with
# y <- 1:100
```

Or just wrap with a list (though that takes a little expression-parsing internally to get the names out):

``` r
reprex({y + 2}, vars = list(y))
```

If you like this feature idea I'll add it to the next PR.

(Fun fact; after I finished this example I used reprex to share it. Works like a charm!)

```R
x <- quote({
  # This is a comment
  a +      b
})

src_n <- src[[length(src)]]

lines <-  attr(src_1, "srcfile")$lines
lines <- lines[seq(src_1[1], src_n[3])]
lines[1] <- substring(lines[1], src_1[5] + 1, nchar(lines[1]))

}
```

Currently the function works in the current directory using a base filename along the lines of 08-25-2015_REPREX_gh. It keeps them there if outfiles = TRUE.

I suspect that:
- Most users won't want to keep the input and output files, especially since the goal is to get it into GitHub or SO
- Those that do would be at least as happy providing their own filename (so they can refer to it later); while they can specify 

Thus, I'd propose working in a temporary file unless the user specifically provides an output file base (in which case the .R and .md will be appended). This saves some of the utility work in the reprex function, and lets the user choose the filename without being appended with a date.

title: Images
description:
Images are one of the most difficult aspects of a reproducible example; they tend to stop an answer flow cold, as it involves saving an image, uploading it to something like Imgur, then pasting in a link to that.

Is there _anything_ we can do to make this process easier? The ideal solution would be for knitr to upload generated figures to Imgur (which could be done with a custom knitr hook), but you need an API token to upload programmatically, which is an obstacle.

Perhaps at least the figures generated could be stuck in some easy-to-reach place so they can be uploaded.

(I know I've generated a pile of issues today; most of them are just for me to come back to later)
